title: Intervention Follow-Up, Outcome Evidence and Confounding

content.overview: An intervention is not successful because it was completed. Follow-up compares comparable pre/post evidence, expected response timing, new spread, incidence, severity and relevant confounders. Where evidence is incomplete, the correct conclusion may be unresolved rather than success or failure.

vocabulary.definition: Pre-intervention observation set used for a defensible comparison.
A changing factor that can distort attribution of an observed outcome to the intervention.
Defined evidence used to judge whether the intended response occurred.

sections.title: Define what improvement would look like
sections.body: Before evaluating response, identify the intended measurable outcome: reduced new detections, lower incidence, lower severity, reduced trap counts, constrained spread, or another authorized program metric.

sections.title: Use repeated comparable rounds
sections.body: One clean leaf or one low trap is not control evidence when the multi-round trend disagrees. Evaluate enough comparable locations and rounds to support the scope of the conclusion.

sections.title: Document confounding instead of forcing attribution
sections.body: Sanitation changes, environmental corrections, crop removal, altered sampling effort or overlapping controls can affect the apparent outcome. Record them and limit causal language to what the evidence supports.

workedExamples: Trap counts fall 60%, but half the traps were removed; the apparent improvement cannot be interpreted without correcting for sampling effort.

Incidence falls after an authorized biological release, while affected crop is also removed and humidity is corrected; report improvement but do not attribute the whole effect to one intervention without evidence.
commonMistakes: Calling control success from one observation.
Ignoring simultaneous environmental or sanitation changes.
Moving the follow-up date until the numbers look better.
content.practicalApplication: For an intervention record, define baseline, expected outcome, follow-up schedule, comparable measures, confounders and the criteria for continue/hold/escalate review.
content.summary: Treatment follow-up measures outcomes against a comparable baseline and makes uncertainty visible.
